messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Things feel like they’re holding for now—security’s steady, the banks are still open, and no one’s panicking—but the cracks are there if you know where to look. The real question isn’t whether the regime’s strong, but how long it can keep pretending everything’s fine while the people who actually run things whisper behind closed doors."*"
Sender 2: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are getting harder to ignore—even the birds are singing louder than usual. The usual players are moving their pieces quietly, but the board feels heavier than it did last month. Keep your eyes open, but don’t let them see you looking."*"
Sender 3: "*"The air feels different—like the ground is shifting under us, but no one’s saying it out loud. The usual signs are all there, but the question isn’t *if* things are moving—it’s whether we’re seeing the real cracks or just the ones they want us to see. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and trust your instincts more than the noise."*"
Sender 4: "*"The walls are cracking, but they’re still standing—just leaning harder. People are testing the air, and the regime’s grip feels looser, but don’t mistake hesitation for weakness. Keep your eyes open, your mouths careful, and your plans ready. The wind’s shifting, but we don’t know yet if it’s a storm or just a breeze."*"
Sender 5: "*"The inner circle’s holding tight, but the money men are moving their families—and not quietly. The streets feel like the calm before something, not the quiet after. Stay sharp, but don’t rush. We’ll know soon enough if this is a storm or just the wind."*"
Sender 6: "*"Looks like they’ve got everything locked down tighter than ever—no cracks, no panic, just the usual show of strength. Even the banks are moving in sync, and the streets are quiet except for the usual distractions. For now, it’s all holding, but we’ll keep watching for the first sign of strain."*"
Sender 7: "*"The walls are still standing, but the foundation’s shifting—some cracks are showing, others are just whispers. The question isn’t if things will hold, but how long, and what happens when the first real push comes. Stay sharp, but don’t let fear make the choice for you."*"
Sender 8: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The usual whispers are quieter than usual, but the cracks in the paint are still there, and no one’s rushing to fix them. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open."*"
Sender 9: "*"The air feels lighter—people are talking more, even laughing in the streets, but the old guard is still holding tight. The memes are getting bolder, the leaks stickier, and the generals’ wives are packing their bags… but the banks keep humming, and the courts just keep ‘pausing.’ They’re not panicking yet—but they’re not sleeping easy either. Stay sharp, but don’t let them see you watching."*"
Sender 10: "*"The walls are holding—firm, even. The cracks we’ve been watching? Mostly just shadows. But the sermons are getting sharper, and the warehouses are full. If anything’s coming, it’s not today. Still, keep your eyes open—quiet doesn’t always mean safe."*"
Sender 11: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—elites are quiet, the military’s just going through the motions, and even the banks are holding their breath. Nothing’s breaking yet, but the cracks are showing in the little things: trash piles, slow permits, whispers where there used to be silence. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this could go either way."*"
Sender 12: "*"The air feels lighter than it has in months—checkpoints are quiet, the markets are calm, and even the usual whispers have gone still. The regime’s not just holding on; it’s betting big on staying power, and for now, the numbers seem to be on its side. But let’s keep our eyes open—quiet doesn’t always mean safe."*"
Sender 13: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are getting harder to ignore—people are whispering again, but no one’s ready to shout yet. The regime’s playing defense, not offense, and that’s either smart or desperate. Either way, we should assume they’re listening closer than ever."*"
Sender 14: "*"The walls are holding—maybe too well. The usual cracks aren’t showing, but the quiet ones are starting to hum. Keep your ears open, but don’t let anyone see you listening."*"
Sender 15: "*"Things feel quieter than they have in a while—too quiet, maybe. The usual grumblings are still there, but nothing’s boiling over yet. Still, don’t let the calm fool you—underneath, the machine’s still running, and we all know how fragile that can be."*"
Sender 16: "*"The air feels lighter than it has in months—checkpoints are quiet, the markets are busy, and even the old guard is singing the same tune. But the pharmacist’s stash and those embassy warnings? Let’s not get too comfortable. The machine’s still running, but we all know how fragile the gears can be."*"
Sender 17: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but the cracks are showing—payments are late, the security forces are gearing up, and even the festivals feel like they’re running on borrowed time. Keep your circles tight, stay sharp, and trust your instincts if something feels off—especially with the tech. We’ll talk more in person soon."*"
Sender 18: "*"Things feel like they’re holding for now, but the cracks are starting to show—small things, like the way the usual watchdogs have gone quiet or how even the most cautious among us are saying the same thing: no one knows which way this will tip. Let’s stay sharp, but not so sharp that we draw attention—just keep our eyes open and our ears to the ground. The regime’s still standing, but standing isn’t the same as steady."*"
Sender 19: "*"The air feels thick with whispers, but the walls are still standing—just reinforced. The usual players are still at the table, shuffling the deck, and the lights haven’t flickered yet. Keep your heads down, but don’t forget to listen."*"
Sender 20: "*"The air feels heavy but not yet stormy—elites are whispering but no one’s stepping forward, and the streets are tired, not angry. The markets are steady, but the cracks in the system are getting harder to ignore. For now, we hold, but we watch."*"
Sender 21: "*"The air feels different—less like a storm coming, more like the ground shifting underfoot. The cracks are small, but they’re there, and the regime’s reactions are slower than they used to be. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t the time to bet everything, just to be ready."*"
Sender 22: "*"Looks like the regime’s dug in deeper than we thought—pay’s up, bonds are selling, and even the usual cracks in the script have vanished. People are talking, but no one’s moving yet, and the banks are still humming along. Stay sharp, but don’t hold your breath—this could last longer than we hoped."*"
Sender 23: "*"The air feels different now—like the ground’s shifting under us, but no one’s saying it out loud. Even the landlord’s asking about exit plans, and you know what that means. Stay sharp, but keep it quiet—we’re not alone, but we’re not safe either."*"
Sender 24: "*"Looks like they’re tightening the screws, but not because they’re panicking—more like they’re making sure the machine keeps running smoothly. The crowds are at the stadium, not the streets, and the elites are all holding hands in public. Still, the foreign friends are watching like hawks, so let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—this isn’t over, but it’s not breaking yet either."*"
Sender 25: "*"Things feel like they’re balanced on a knife’s edge—no one’s running for the exits yet, but no one’s fully settled either. The air’s different, like everyone’s holding their breath, waiting to see which way the wind blows next."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
